why: A repository declares its webhook senders in `[signals.sources.<name>]` of its
tracked `.tick/runners.toml` (tick 0vb). That table has two readers: `tk`, which
validates it at author time so a repository learns its config is wrong from the
CLI rather than from a delivery silently refused three weeks later; and the
factory Worker, which ACTS on it — it is the one holding the request, and the
declaration decides whether an unauthenticated POST becomes work.
Two readers of one format is exactly the bug this repository has already paid
for once: a fix landed in TypeScript only, the Go half kept minting unusable
records, and both suites were green because each was internally consistent. So
both read these cases from one file.
`accepted` is what both readers must accept. `refused` means neither may:
the declaration is unusable and saying so is the only safe answer, because the
alternative — ignoring the part it could not read — is a fail-OPEN webhook door.
cloud/factory/test/repo-config.test.ts runs them through the Worker's reader;

cases.name: no signals table
cases.why: The 99% path: a repository that ingests nothing declares nothing.

cases.name: a minimal declaration
cases.why: Everything required and nothing else: a scheme, a dedup key, a title.
cases.toml:
version = 2

[roles.implement]
kind = "claude"

[signals.sources.sentry]
secret = "SIGNAL_SECRET_SENTRY"
header = "sentry-hook-signature"
external_ref = "data.issue.id"
title = "data.issue.title"

cases.name: a full declaration
cases.why: Every optional key at a legal value, including a non-default scheme.
cases.toml:
version = 2

[roles.implement]
kind = "claude"

[signals.sources.statuspage]
secret = "SIGNAL_SECRET_STATUSPAGE"
header = "x-statuspage-signature"
algorithm = "hmac-sha512"
encoding = "base64"
prefix = "v1="
external_ref = "incident.id"
title = "incident.name"
description = "incident.body"
type = "chore"
priority = 3
labels = ["statuspage", "ops"]

cases.why: A registry, not a single sender.

cases.name: an unknown key in a source
cases.why: Fail closed by key. Ignoring one is how a typo'd `header` becomes an unauthenticated door.

cases.name: an unknown key under [signals]
cases.why: The container table fails closed too — `[signals].allow_all` must never be silently dropped.

cases.name: __proto__ as a key

cases.why: runners.toml is tracked and usually public: `secret` is the NAME of a Worker secret, never a secret.

cases.why: `title` names WHERE the value comes from. Prose there resolves to nothing at delivery time; refusing it here is the legible failure.

cases.name: no external_ref
cases.why: Without the sender's own stable id, every redelivery would file another tick.

cases.name: no secret
cases.why: An unsigned door is not a door. A declaration without a scheme must not load at all.
